description: binwave: MySQL to ClickHouse replication. Works with Prometheus and with PMM (pick its metrics data source).

panels.title: Replicating
panels.description: 1 while the service replicates. 0 while starting or stopping, paused, stopped by a failure, or degraded.

panels.title: Degraded
panels.description: Requests to ClickHouse keep failing and are being retried: the service is up, nothing gets through, the position stands still. Clears by itself on the first success.

panels.title: Failed
panels.description: Replication is stopped by a transaction that could not be replicated. Needs an operator: binwave replication status, then resume (retry) or resume --skip-transactions / --gtid-next.

panels.title: Paused
panels.description: Replication is paused by an operator (binwave replication pause) or not started (replication.autostart: false).

panels.title: Quarantined tables
panels.description: Tables set aside because they cannot be replicated; each falls behind the source until it is resynchronized and released (binwave tables list).

panels.title: Degraded for
panels.description: How long requests to ClickHouse have been failing without a success; 0 when they are not.

panels.title: Lag
panels.description: How far ClickHouse is behind the source: 0 while the source has nothing more to send, otherwise the age of the oldest change not yet written and saved. During an initial load a large lag is expected — see the Initial load row.

panels.title: Position age
panels.description: Seconds since the source committed the last transaction the saved position covers (does not depend on binwave's own lag logic), and since the position was last saved.

panels.title: Transactions per second
panels.description: Transactions read from the source binlog, including those of tables that are not replicated.

panels.title: Rows per second
panels.description: Rows produced from the source's changes (an update produces two) and rows accepted by ClickHouse after duplicates within a batch were collapsed.

panels.title: Rows per insert
panels.description: How full the batches are. A handful of rows per insert means the cost is the round-trip and the fsync of each insert, not the rows: raise buffer.catchup_flush_interval while catching up, or look at why the stream is slow.

panels.title: Buffered rows
panels.description: Rows waiting in memory to be written to ClickHouse.

panels.title: Buffered bytes
panels.description: Estimated size of the rows waiting in memory; reading the source pauses at buffer.max_memory (backpressure).

panels.title: Inserts in flight
panels.description: Average number of inserts running at once. Close to buffer.insert_parallelism: ClickHouse is the limit. Well below it while the lag grows: the limit is before the inserts (reading or converting the stream).

panels.title: Insert latency
panels.description: How long ClickHouse takes to accept a batch, retries included.

panels.title: Retries per second
panels.description: Requests to ClickHouse that failed and are retried. overload: the server asks for less load (too many parts); transient: network or a server that is restarting.

panels.title: Initial load
panels.description: Share of the tables of the initial load that are in place (visible in ClickHouse). No data when there is no initial load.

panels.title: Initial load by state
panels.description: Tables of the initial load: loaded (in place), reading (a slot reads its chunks), waiting_for_stream (read, replaced once the stream reaches the point it was read at), waiting_for_slot (not started). A growing waiting_for_stream means the stream, not the reading, is the limit.

panels.title: Resyncs and rebuilds
panels.description: Tables resynchronized right now on an operator's request or by tables.autoresync (the initial load is counted on the left), and tables rebuilt under a new sort key: while a rebuild runs no table is replicated and the lag grows.

panels.title: Rows read by resyncs
panels.description: Rows read from the source by the initial load and by resyncs.

panels.title: Resyncs finished
panels.description: Tables resynchronized and replaced, those tables.autoresync resynchronized on its own, and its failed attempts.

panels.title: Value adjustments
panels.description: Values replaced by a documented rule (zero dates and the like) instead of converted exactly. Not an error, but the data in ClickHouse differs from the source there.

panels.title: Rows skipped by quarantine
panels.description: Changes dropped because their table is quarantined: that table falls behind the source by this much.

panels.title: Source and schema events
panels.description: Reconnects of the binlog connection, reads of the source for a resync or the initial load that failed and are retried, transactions skipped by an operator, and destructive DDL left unapplied (ddl.mode additive, partition operations).

panels.title: CPU
panels.description: CPU time used by the process, in cores.

panels.title: Memory
panels.description: Resident memory of the process and the live Go heap.

panels.title: Goroutines
panels.description: Goroutines of the process; a number that keeps growing is a leak.

panels.title: Version
panels.description: Version of the running binary.

panels.title: Uptime
panels.description: Time since the process started.

panels.title: Startup failures
panels.description: Failed attempts to start, before the service became ready.

list.name: instance_label
list.label: Instance by
list.description: The label that tells instances apart: instance in Prometheus; in PMM, where instance is the ID of the agent, node_name (the host) or service_name.
